about.budget: the four derived files together stay under 200 KB (spec §6), written as compact JSON (indented they would be about 237 KB); excerpts are capped at 240 (step), 400 (reply) and 120 (args, task) characters
about.not_recorded: {"recorded": false, "command": ...} where a trace is missing, never a number
about.notes: per pattern: did Python and Go make the same number of model calls on each ticket recorded in both
about.reply: the pattern's final reply (summary for parallel, final for evaluate_optimize), at most 400 characters

rulings.R62: cost and latency come from the recording: the sum of the trace's proxy_calls cost_usd and ms, served again on replay; never what one run paid (spent, cost_usd) or measured locally (a record's ms)
rulings.R64: the ledger keeps input, cache-write, cache-read and output tokens apart; cache writes are priced at 1.25x and cache reads at 0.10x the input price, so prompt caching shows as a lower cost
rulings.R66: the gate stays as built (0.7 minus the 1/sqrt(n) band); with 13 tickets no engine clears it. That is the real result and is shown as it is, never adjusted

about.steps: each trace record in order: model (agent, role, tokens, cost and ms from the matching proxy_calls entry, result: what that call produced, at most 240 characters) and tool (name, args); a parallel pattern's tool args come from its lookups, an orchestrator's workers' tool args are not logged (null). A worker's result sits on its last call
about.what: PatternStepper: the five hand-built patterns, step by step, in Python (hand) and Go (hand-go)

chain.note: Python and Go made the same number of model calls on every ticket

evaluate_optimize.note: Python and Go made different numbers of model calls (t061: Python 6, Go 2): the recorded replies differed (a judge passed sooner, a worker took more tool turns), so a loop ran a different number of times

orchestrate.note: Python and Go made different numbers of model calls (t001: Python 9, Go 8; t061: Python 7, Go 8): the recorded replies differed (a judge passed sooner, a worker took more tool turns), so a loop ran a different number of times

parallel.note: Python and Go made the same number of model calls on every ticket
